reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing linear Kalman filtering with a learned Mamba selective state-space model (SSM) that captures complex motion dynamics. The model takes bounding box sequences [x, y, w, h] and maps them through a linear projection followed by two Mamba blocks, producing a latent motion representation. This is then decoded via an MLP head into predicted boxes. The key advancement is in the SSM formulation, which approximates continuous dynamics via selective discretization (Eq. 3–4), allowing for efficient training while preserving temporal coherence. Unlike traditional Kalman filters, this approach handles nonlinearity and occlusions better. A secondary MLP embeds trajectories into a shared space for clustering, enabling effective tracklet merging post-tracking. The system achieves 28.8 FPS inference speed on a single GPU, making it suitable for real-time broadcast analysis. However, performance degrades when motion becomes highly irregular or when detection quality drops significantly.
